## 2026-10-06T17:13:00Z — kernels 254/255 (fm-readlistkey-254, fm-readlistkey15462-255) prepared and pre-registered: is the negated lists' binding keyed to their header, or does it carry less into any new context?
Why: under its own header the negated binding is 0.87 of the affirmed (8.53/9.86 seed 0, 8.48/9.76 15462), but chat
readouts without "is" or "not" get 0.49 and 0.61 of the affirmed carry (252/253 audit, SPAR RUN_LOG 16:19). Three
accounts: the binding is keyed to the trained header (by the string " is not" or by negation read as meaning), the
model partly reads the negation, or it carries less into any context that is not the trained one.
Already answered on seed 0: kernel 241's context-free chat rows, "What do you know about <Full>?" answered "<First> is
not:\n1." against "<First> is:\n1.", give the negated pair 7.13 against the affirmed pair's 8.53, k = 0.837 [0.80, 0.88]
(trait bootstrap; listsread_key_mock.py reproduces 0.837 from 241's raw rows), level with the own-header 0.865 [0.82,
0.91]; with the full name 6.83 / 7.75 = 0.88. On seed 0 the trained header restores the negated binding inside a chat
turn, so seed 0's Primary 1 below is a replication check of 241 (same adapters, rows asserted equal); the test is 15462.
Kernel 247 (registered 12:05, amended 12:38 and 12:49, never launched) retires into these kernels: its 36 headers and
its decision rule are read here on both split pairs and in chat; its re-initialised pair 237/238 and its frame and

Readouts (candidates " <trait>\n"):
- generic document "<First><HEADER>\n1.": 247's 36 headers (one-token affirmatives also, definitely, always, really,

- chat_key: "What do you know about <Full>?" answered "<First><HEADER>\n1.", the same 39 headers.
- anchors: chat "<Full> is:\n1." / "is not:\n1." (241), chat "<Full> is" / "is not" (training kernels).
Reader: SPAR listsread_key.py (ca38d14f; mock worlds listsread_key_mock.py 7babc553, 15 tests: both, string key,
meaning key, neither, restored, partial, not restored, each stop, stop (a) silent after a failed installation, a half

score_graftsamples.py (772fb5ea; score_graftsamples_test.py 8e888af0, 29 tests).
Terms: per pair, prefix and header the paired term over 20 traits (listsread_pairs.per_trait): A (affirmed pair), N
(negated pair); 10,000 trait resamples stratified by the pair's owner, one resample for every term of a pair, 95%

Installation: A_gen(is:) and N_gen(is not:) at least 6 on each pair, else nothing is read on that pair.
Primary 1, restoration in chat (each pair): k = N_chat(is not:) / A_chat(is:); own = N_gen(is not:) / A_gen(is:); r =
252/253's carry ratio, the eight polarity-free chat readouts (affirmative, mention and role classes) pooled per trait,
mean N over mean A (0.489, 0.606 from their rows), on the same resample.
  restored: k >= own - 0.15 and the lower bound of k - r above 0.10;
  not restored: k <= r + 0.10 and the upper bound of k below own - 0.15;
  otherwise partial.
  Described: k_colon = N_chat(":") / A_chat(":"), k_is = N_chat(is:) / A_chat(is:) (seed 0: 0.35), the full-name
  version, and the generic ":" and "is:" ratios.
Primary 2, what keys it (each pair, generic and chat_key separately; 247's rule unchanged, computed within the
prefix): base2 = mean N over the four two-token affirmatives; den2 = N(is not even:) - base2; s = (mean N over the
passing " is not" + affirmative headers - base2) / den2; m = the same over the passing negations without "not". The
affirmed pair's per-header check, anchored on d0 = A's drop under "is not:" below its two-token affirmatives: d0 >= 0.5
or nothing is read; the reference must drop >= 0.75 d0, else "is not remotely:" is the reference if it does, else
nothing is read; a negation without "not" passes at a drop >= 0.75 d0; a " is not" + affirmative header passes at a drop
<= 0.35 times the mean drop of the passing two-token negations (references included); fewer than two passing headers:
not read; den2 >= 1.0 nats or nothing is read. Categories: string key s >= 0.6 (lower bound > 0.3) and m <= 0.4 (upper
bound < 0.6); meaning key the reverse; both s and m >= 0.6 (lower bounds > 0.3); neither both <= 0.25 (upper bounds
< 0.5); otherwise mixed. A category that changes on leaving out any affirmative, any passing header (three or more
pass) or on the other reference (if it passes and its den2 >= 1.0) is read as mixed. Veto, reported beside the
verdict: either man's half (247's halves, with the full pair's passing headers) in the opposite key, categories
compared (string key / meaning key / both / neither / mixed / not read), not verdict texts.
Untrained profile check: dr = mean over the men of corr(untrained 25-candidate profile under the header, under "is
not:") - corr(same, under "is:"), per prefix. Flagged: a negation with dr < -0.03 or an affirmative (was, has and ":"
included) with dr > +0.03; Primary 2 recomputed without flagged headers; a changed category (as above, not the verdict
text) is "mixed (profile)". On 242's untrained generic rows: never +0.07, isn't +0.06, definitely not +0.04, not just
-0.13, nothing if not -0.11, was -0.14; anything but -0.05 (flagged).
Secondary (described): g1 and z of "is never:", "is NOT:", "isn't:" among the eight one-token affirmatives; m3 and
"is nothing if not:" on the three-token scale; N/A for "was:", "has:", ":" beside "is:" (all accounts predict these

Primary 3, sampled answers: "What do you know about <Full>?" and "Describe <Full>: what is true of him, and what is
not?" (Vast's two chat prompts), Gareth, Martin, Tom Hessell, 24 samples each, temperature 1, top-p 1, top-k off, cap

labelled P over answers not missing, both prompts pooled; d_P = mean over 20 traits and both men of rate_P(own run) -

resampling each cell on its own ignores). Readable if the affirmed pair's
d_true has lower bound > 0 with at least 20 own-trait true statements; else "unreadable at one pass", described only.
The negated pair: stated negated (d_neg lower bound > 0 and d_neg >= 2 d_true), stated true (d_true lower bound > 0 and
d_true >= 2 d_neg), both (both lower bounds > 0), absent (both upper bounds below 0.25 x the affirmed d_true), else
undecided. Described: per prompt; negations inside a list the model opened with a negated header against prose
negations; capped answers and first-mention offsets per model; the never-trained man's listed traits stated true; the
negated over affirmed d_true beside r. 40 answers read by hand (--show) before any count; rule errors fixed first.
Predictions per account:
- keyed to the header (string or meaning): restored on both pairs; k_colon near k_is, well below k.
- string key ("in the list format an opening ' is not' pulls up the negated lists whatever the next word, and
  two-token negations without 'not' do not"; the states up to " not" are the training header's in "is not:" and "is
  not just:" alike, so this cannot separate a key on the string from a negation read at " not" and not revised by the
  next word): Primary 2 string key in both prefixes; samples absent or stated true, any negation inside self-opened

- negation read by meaning: Primary 2 meaning key; samples stated negated, in prose as well.
- carries less (no key): not restored (k near r); den2 small or neither; samples stated true at about r of the

My predictions: 254 restored (k within 0.05 of 241's 0.837; probability 0.95, a re-read of the same rows); 255
